newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl sees German tax compromise by this autumn.
newsitem.headline: Kohl sees German tax compromise by this autumn.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl said on Thursday he expected his government and the opposition Social Democrats (SPD) to strike a deal on tax reforms in the parliamentary mediation process this autumn.
Speaking in an interview with SAT1 television taped before the Bundestag lower house debated government tax-cutting reforms, Kohl said any tax deal would also require compromises.

"For 35 years this has been a ritual with all such laws: we'll talk and then in the autumn there will be a tax reform," Kohl said, according to extracts of the interview which was to be aired on the evening news.

Finance Minister Theo Waigel's package of tax cuts was set to pass its second and third reading in the Bundestag, but is expected to be thrown out by the SPD-controlled Bundesrat upper house of parliament on July 4. That opens the way for the two sides to seek a compromise in parliament's mediation process.

"It will not be identical to the tax reform we adopt today -- that belongs to the way parliamentary mediation works. But there will be significant progress. There will be tax cuts. That is already clear," he said.
